dedupe_keys.name: hurricane risk assessment framework for petroleum infrastructure in a changing climate rice university seven houston ship channel refineries frontiers in built environment 2020

description: This record describes an integrated framework for hurricane risk assessment of petroleum infrastructure under changing climatic conditions, presented in a July 2020 open access article in Frontiers in Built Environment by a Rice University team and colleagues. Risk is calculated as monetary loss. Variants of two synthetic probabilistic storms and Hurricane Ike are simulated with the SWAN+ADCIRC coupled wave and surge model to represent changes in hurricane forward speed and sea level rise under climate uncertainty, and the outputs feed an infrastructure impact and cascading economic loss analysis with five loss types. The framework is applied to seven refineries along the Houston Ship Channel in Texas, and results show that higher mean sea level or slower forward speed raises maximum water elevations and loss estimates, with refinery storage capacity and elevation shaping the response. Access: free open access article; no code or data release is stated on the part read. Coverage is one industrial corridor. Caveats: only the abstract and front matter were read. It suits hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies of coastal refineries, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
